Read in and wrangle the data.

```{r}
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(janitor)

# SATP data
satp_village_df <- read_csv("../data/satp_clean.csv") |>
  mutate(across(state:constituency, str_to_lower)) |>
  rename(
    town_village = village_name,
    sub_district = block
    ) |>
  drop_na(town_village) |>
  mutate(state = case_when(
    state == "kerela" ~ "kerala",
    TRUE ~ state
  ))

# Village names and identifiers
village_names_df <- read_csv("data-large/villagenamesdataset.csv") |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(across(!village_code, str_to_lower))
```

Does not work. Crashes because data frames are too big. 

Try looping through states and doing one state at a time.

```{r}
library(purrr)
library(fuzzyjoin)
library(dplyr)
library(stringdist)

# Create a list of unique states from satp_village_df
states <- unique(satp_village_df$state)

# Function to process a chunk of data for a state
process_state_chunk <- function(state, chunk, names_state_subset) {
  fuzzy_matches <- stringdist_left_join(chunk,
                                        names_state_subset,
                                        by = c("district", "town_village"),
                                        max_dist = 1,  
                                        method = "lv")
  
  # Process each incident_number to find the best match within the chunk
  incident_results <- fuzzy_matches |>
    group_by(incident_number) |>
    slice_min(stringdist(district.x, district.y, method = "jw") + 
              stringdist(town_village.x, town_village.y, method = "jw"), 
              with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ungroup()
  
  return(incident_results)
}

# Function to process an entire state
process_state <- function(state) {
  cat("Processing state:", state, "\n")
  
  satp_state_subset <- satp_village_df |> filter(state == tolower(!!state))
  names_state_subset <- village_names_df |> filter(state == tolower(!!state))
  
  chunk_size <- 100
  num_chunks <- ceiling(nrow(satp_state_subset) / chunk_size)
  
  cat("Number of rows for", state, ":", nrow(satp_state_subset), "\n")
  cat("Number of rows in village_names for", state, ":", nrow(names_state_subset), "\n")
  cat("Number of chunks for", state, ":", num_chunks, "\n")
  
  state_results <- map(1:num_chunks, function(i) {
    start_idx <- (i - 1) * chunk_size + 1
    end_idx <- min(i * chunk_size, nrow(satp_state_subset))
    chunk <- satp_state_subset[start_idx:end_idx, ]
    
    cat("Processing chunk", i, "of", num_chunks, "for state", state, "\n")
    chunk_result <- process_state_chunk(state, chunk, names_state_subset)
    return(chunk_result)
  })
  
  state_result <- bind_rows(state_results)
  cat("Completed processing for state:", state, "\n")
  return(state_result)
}

# Main processing function
process_all_states <- function(states) {
  cat("Starting to process all states\n")
  
  # Diagnostic: Print row counts by state
  state_counts <- satp_village_df |>
    group_by(state) |>
    summarise(count = n()) |>
    arrange(desc(count))
  
  cat("Row counts by state:\n")
  print(state_counts)
  
  state_results <- map(states, safely(process_state))
  
  cat("Finished processing all states\n")
  
  successful_results <- map(state_results, "result")
  errors <- map(state_results, "error")
  
  states_with_errors <- names(errors[!sapply(errors, is.null)])
  if (length(states_with_errors) > 0) {
    cat("States with errors:", paste(states_with_errors, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }
  
  final_df <- bind_rows(successful_results) |>
  relocate(incident_number, state.x, state.y, district.x, district.y, sub_district.x, sub_district.y, town_village.x, town_village.y, village_code)

  
  # Count and report duplicates
  duplicate_counts <- final_df |>
    group_by(incident_number) |>
    summarise(count = n()) |>
    filter(count > 1)
  
  cat("Number of incident numbers with duplicates:", nrow(duplicate_counts), "\n")
  cat("Total number of duplicate entries:", sum(duplicate_counts$count) - nrow(duplicate_counts), "\n")
  
  # Report on the distribution of duplicates
  duplicate_distribution <- duplicate_counts |>
    group_by(count) |>
    summarise(frequency = n()) |>
    arrange(desc(count))
  
  cat("\nDistribution of duplicates:\n")
  print(duplicate_distribution)
  
  cat("\nNumber of rows in final_df:", nrow(final_df), "\n")
  return(final_df)
}

# Run the processing
final_df <- process_all_states(states)
```

Calculate number of unmatched cases

```{r}
# Count total number of cases
total_cases <- nrow(satp_village_df)

# Count number of unmatched cases (either village or district)
unmatched_cases <- final_df |> 
  filter(is.na(town_village.y) | is.na(district.y)) |> 
  nrow()

# Calculate the percentage of matched cases
percent_matched <- (1 - (unmatched_cases / total_cases)) * 100


cat("Total cases:", total_cases, "\n")
cat("Unmatched cases (village or district):", unmatched_cases, "\n")
cat("Percentage of cases matched:", percent_matched, "%\n")

# Check for districts in satp_village_df that never had any match
unmatched_districts <- satp_village_df |> 
  filter(!district %in% final_df$district.x) |> 
  distinct(district)

cat("Districts with no matches:\n")
print(unmatched_districts)
```

## Notes

Query: what is the ground truth for determining how good these matches 
are? Could be the basis of an article.
  - 1200 or so randomly selected cases
  - matched by hand to official government list
  - what kinds of biases do we see, if any (regional?)
  - what methods of matching produce the best results?
